source.title: Deep Isometric Learning for Visual Recognition
source.authors: Haozhi Qi; Chong You; X. Wang; Yi Ma; J. Malik

record.tranche_reason: The paper trains isometric vanilla convolutional networks and compares initialization, regularization, activation, and depth settings. It reports ImageNet validation accuracy and convergence, rather than training classification error.
record.gate_note: Rows report the paper’s own ImageNet Top-1 results and explicit convergence statements. Cited results from other papers are not included. No CIFAR or training-error measurements are reported.
record.test_reason: The explicit report that very deep plain batch-normalized networks fail to converge bears on V3's depth-related optimization failure. Most extracted rows measure final validation accuracy, which does not establish training-error degradation, training speed, or initialization-dependent trainable depth.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that near-isometry is a central design principle for effective deep-network learning. Their combined recipe trains plain networks beyond 100 layers, while residual ISONets achieve competitive ImageNet performance without normalization. These conclusions do not establish initialization-specific training-speed effects.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses isometric convolution initialization and regularization with SReLU, and reports ImageNet validation accuracy and convergence rather than CIFAR training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth and the presence of Delta initialization, orthogonal regularization, SReLU, and dropout change reported accuracy or convergence. Orthogonal-regularization coefficient also changes accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: The full isometric recipe trains SReLU networks without normalization or shortcuts through 101 layers; initialization, activation, regularization, and dropout ablations change final validation accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A combined near-isometric initialization, activation, and training-time regularization recipe enables competitive ImageNet validation performance in plain convolutional networks through 101 layers.

record.problems: Reports Top-1 validation accuracy rather than training classification error; no CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 results. The extremely deep vanilla-network convergence statements are reported through N/A table entries defined as non-convergence or accuracy below 40.

untested.parts: All parts: CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
All parts: two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious minima, and extra student neurons.

Numerical training-error comparisons, longer-training controls, CIFAR-10, very deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup training without normalization. ISONet uses SReLU and training-time orthogonal regularization.

Initialization-dependent learning speed and trainable depth; activation-matched initialization comparisons; orthogonal versus equal-variance Gaussian tanh networks; and 10,000-layer convolutional networks. Final validation-accuracy ablations do not establish these outcomes.
All parts: stability thresholds, loss transients, curvature, sharpness, and divergence relative to those thresholds.
Accuracy gain per training time or step, learning-rate tolerance comparisons, and Fixup speed or stability relative to batch normalization. Table 5 reports final validation accuracy.

missing.what: Depth comparators for the qualitative V3 result: plain batch-normalized networks achieve 68.98%, 69.43%, and 70.00% validation accuracy at 18, 34, and 50 layers, while 101 layers is N/A. Standard ResNet achieves 77.37% at 101 layers. Record these as validation/convergence context, without converting them into training-error measurements.

record.verdict_notes: The original V3 challenge label has the direction backward: failure of very deep plain networks is consistent with degradation. R23 also misreads Table 4. Validation-performance differences and regularization sensitivity do not justify the record's V4 verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, training classification error, and the stated size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and spurious minima.

The paper tests deep plain convolutional networks on ImageNet, but not the version’s ImageNet/CIFAR-10 training-error comparison of plain batch-normalized networks with and without identity shortcuts. Its deep plain models use isometric design; it does not test the stated very deep tanh setup.

Tests Delta initialization and orthogonal regularization in convolutional networks, including depth and convergence. Does not test the listed activation-matched initializations, learning speed, or orthogonal versus Gaussian weights at equal variance.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature, and sharpness.
Batch normalization’s training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training speed or stability.

rows.subject: 34-layer ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained on ImageNet with ReLU, Kaiming initialization, and no orthogonal regularization; regular ResNet baseline.
rows.note: Accuracy is reported; this row does not establish training error.
rows.check: Validation accuracy alone does not measure V3's training-error or convergence comparison.

rows.subject: Vanilla
rows.operation_detail: ResNet-style network without BatchNorm or skip connections.
rows.note: The paper says the plain vanilla network cannot be easily optimized; it identifies 34 layers as the deepest vanilla network it found trainable.
rows.check: This network lacks batch normalization; its validation accuracy does not measure V3's specified comparison.

rows.subject: Vanilla network with orthogonal convolution only
rows.operation_detail: Enforced convolution isometry, without the full ISONet components.
rows.note: The text says convolution isometry alone yields approximately 46% Top-1 accuracy.
rows.check: Final validation accuracy does not measure initialization-dependent training speed or trainable depth. Describe this as convolution isometry without SReLU, rather than assuming orthogonal regularization is its only component.

rows.subject: Vanilla network with isometric activation only
rows.operation_detail: Used SReLU without the full ISONet components.
rows.note: Table 1 identifies this as an ablation; the text says activation isometry alone cannot achieve good performance.
rows.check: An activation ablation measured by final validation accuracy does not establish V4's initialization effect.

rows.subject: Vanilla network without Delta initialization
rows.operation_detail: ISONet ablation omitting Delta initialization.
rows.note: The text reports an approximately 2-point drop when Delta initialization is removed.
rows.check: The 68.50% versus 70.45% comparison measures final validation performance, not learning speed or maximum trainable depth.

rows.subject: Vanilla network without orthogonal regularization
rows.operation_detail: ISONet ablation omitting orthogonal regularization.
rows.note: The text reports an approximately 2-point drop when orthogonal regularization is removed.
rows.check: Removing training-time regularization and measuring validation accuracy does not isolate V4's initialization effect.

rows.subject: ISONet
rows.operation_detail: Trained vanilla convolutional network using SReLU, Delta initialization, and orthogonal regularization.
rows.note: The paper says ISONet can be effectively trained without normalization or skip connections.
rows.check: The combined initialization, activation, and regularization recipe demonstrates trainability, but does not measure V3's specified networks or isolate V4's initialization-dependent speed or depth.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports competitive Top-1 accuracy for a trained vanilla network without normalization or skip connections (R16, R20). This is evidence of deep trainability in this setting, but not of the version’s training-error comparison.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: 50- and 101-layer standard vanilla networks on ImageNet
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports non-convergence or accuracy below 40 for plain networks with or without BatchNorm at these depths (R21–R24).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The full isometric recipe achieves the reported accuracy and is trainable beyond 100 layers; removing components lowers the 34-layer result (R3–R7, R13–R20).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported accuracy is lower with no regularization or the largest tested coefficient than with intermediate coefficients (R8–R12).
